blocks.text: Origin / creation. Governance established Courts to decide disputes involving forks, reconstructions, dormant claims, stolen identity, memory transfer, and obligations across change.
Identity / human status. Artificial civic institution composed of rotating judges, witnesses, interpreters, and affected claimants. No permanent ruler controlled it.
Importance. Courts replaced binary sameness verdicts with responsibility-centered inquiry: which experience continued, whose consent was missing, and what harm would follow from forcing one answer.
Decline or transformation. Courts distributed across worlds, became strained by preservation panic, and in Era Two translated only limited protections into automatic Codex safeguards.
Final status / surviving function. The complete institution dissolved. Identity boundaries, fork protections, and the Ancestral Claim Prohibition remain as inherited functions.
